title: Affine finite-presentation Isom space for relatively flat modules with proper support
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] of finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: it is locally of finite presentation on etale charts, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules on small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and canonical tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $M,N$ be finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, both flat over $B$ and both with support proper over $B$. Finitely presented means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. Relative flatness means that on etale scheme charts the module stalks are flat over the local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means that each module is isomorphic to $i_*E$ for some closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ proper over $B$ and some finite type quasi-coherent module $E$ on $Z$, where finite type means etale locally finitely generated [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. For each scheme $T\to B$, put $X_T=X\times_BT$ and let $M_T,N_T$ be the tensor pullbacks. Then the functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal O_{X_T}}(M_T,N_T)$, with transition maps given by tensor pullback of isomorphisms, is represented by an algebraic space $I\to B$ affine and of finite presentation. The representing bijections are natural in every scheme $T\to B$. Affine means that every base change to an affine scheme over $B$ is an affine scheme; finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness as above. No properness or flatness of $f$, and no Noetherian hypothesis on $B$, is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-hom-affine] to the four ordered pairs $(M,N),(N,M),(M,M),(N,N)$. In every application the source is finitely presented, and the target is finitely presented, flat over $B$, and has proper support by the hypotheses on $M,N$. Obtain representing spaces $H=\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)$, $H'=\operatorname{Hom}(N,M)$, $E=\operatorname{Hom}(M,M)$ and $E'=\operatorname{Hom}(N,N)$, each affine and of finite presentation over $B$, with the stated natural identifications on all scheme tests. No property of $f$ beyond finite presentation is used.

Form $P=H'\times_B H$ and $Q=E\times_B E'$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The projection $P\to H$ is the base change of $H'\to B$, and $Q\to E'$ is the base change of $E\to B$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] these projections are affine; by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] they are of finite presentation. Composing them with $H\to B$ and $E'\to B$, respectively, gives $P,Q\to B$ affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] and of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. In particular $q:Q\to B$ is separated by the affine-locality node.

For $T\to B$, send $(v:N_T\to M_T,u:M_T\to N_T)$ to $(v\circ u,u\circ v)\in E(T)\times E'(T)$. Pullback is a functor [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], so it preserves these compositions and identity maps. The canonical comparison of successive tensor pullbacks [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] is natural in module maps, so these formulas commute with every $T'\to T$. They therefore define $c:P\to Q$ and the identity section $\sigma:B\to Q$, since morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The order of the components is essential: $v\circ u$ acts on $M_T$ and $u\circ v$ on $N_T$. The reversed order printed in Tag 08K9 does not have the displayed codomain.

source.place: Tag 08K9, composition map and identity section; corrected component order; Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules) for the canonical pullback comparison.

proof.text: We justify the properties of $\sigma$ without taking a general section lemma as an extra input. For a scheme $T$ and $a:T\to Q$, the pullback of $\Delta_q:Q\to Q\times_BQ$ along $(a,\sigma q a)$ consists of a map $z:T'\to Q$ with $z=a|_{T'}=\sigma q a|_{T'}$. It is naturally $B\times_QT$: the forward map uses $b=q a|_{T'}$, and the reverse map sends $b$ with $\sigma b=a|_{T'}$ to $z=a|_{T'}$. These maps are inverse because $q\sigma=\mathrm{id}_B$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], $q$ is separated, so its diagonal is representable by closed immersions. Thus every scheme test of $\sigma$ is a closed immersion. Such scheme morphisms are affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $\sigma$ is affine by the definition of affine space morphism in [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. The same node gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, of $\sigma$. Since $q$ is of finite presentation, it is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence] to $B\xrightarrow{\sigma}Q\xrightarrow{q}B$: their composite is $\mathrm{id}_B$, which is locally of finite presentation in the chart test of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], because every scheme map $h:U\to V$ between representable etale charts of $B$ with $b\circ h=a$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], hence locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. It follows that $\sigma$ is locally of finite presentation; together with its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness this says it is of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 08K9, identity section: Tag 03KP (lemma-section-immersion), with its diagonal-pullback argument written out, and Tag 05WT (lemma-finite-presentation-permanence).

proof.text: Let $J=P\times_{c,Q,\sigma}B$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $J\to P$ is a base change of $\sigma$; it is affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] and of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Compose with $P\to B$ from Step 2. Affine composition [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] and finite-presentation composition [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] show that $J\to B$ is affine and of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 08K9, displayed fibre product and final conclusion; Tags 03WI, 03WH, 03XR and 03XQ for permanence.

proof.text: For every scheme $T\to B$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $J(T)$ with pairs $(v,u)$ for which $v u=\mathrm{id}_{M_T}$ and $u v=\mathrm{id}_{N_T}$. Send such a pair to the isomorphism $u:M_T\to N_T$, and send an isomorphism $u$ to $(u^{-1},u)$. If $v,w$ are both inverses of $u$, then $v=v(uw)=(vu)w=w$, so the two maps are inverse bijections. For $a:T'\to T$, functoriality of tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] gives $a^*(v)a^*(u)=\mathrm{id}$ and $a^*(u)a^*(v)=\mathrm{id}$. Hence $a^*(v)$ is the inverse of $a^*(u)$. Conjugating by the natural comparison [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] gives exactly the specified $M_{T'},N_{T'}$ and their transition maps. Thus the bijections commute with every base change, proving the asserted representation with $I=J$.

lean.statement: theorem module_isom_affine {S : Scheme.{u}} {X B : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ B) (hf : ProperQuotFinitePresentation f) (M N : X.QCoh) (hMfp : M.obj.IsFinitePresentation) (hNfp : N.obj.IsFinitePresentation) (hMflat : ModuleIsFlatOver f M.obj) (hNflat : ModuleIsFlatOver f N.obj) (hMsupport : ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom ∧ MapIsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ ∃ E : Z.Modules, E.IsQuasicoherent ∧ E.IsFiniteType ∧ Nonempty ((moduleDirectImage i).obj E ≅ M.obj)) (hNsupport : ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom ∧ MapIsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ ∃ E : Z.Modules, E.IsQuasicoherent ∧ E.IsFiniteType ∧ Nonempty ((moduleDirectImage i).obj E ≅ N.obj)) : ∃ (I : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : I ⟶ B), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q ↦ IsAffineHom q.left) p.hom.hom ∧ ProperQuotFinitePresentation p ∧ ∃ e : ∀ T : ProperQuotTest B, {g : yoneda.obj T.left ⟶ I.obj.obj // g ≫ p.hom.hom = T.hom} ≃ ((moduleTensorPullback (properQuotFst f T)).obj M.obj ≅ (moduleTensorPullback (properQuotFst f T)).obj N.obj), ∀ (T' T : ProperQuotTest B) (h : T' ⟶ T) (g : {g : yoneda.obj T.left ⟶ I.obj.obj // g ≫ p.hom.hom = T.hom}) (g' : {g : yoneda.obj T'.left ⟶ I.obj.obj // g ≫ p.hom.hom = T'.hom}), g'.val = yoneda.map h.left ≫ g.val → e T' g' = (properQuotSourceIso f M.obj h).symm ≪≫ (moduleTensorPullback (properQuotFibreMap f h)).mapIso (e T g) ≪≫ properQuotSourceIso f N.obj h
